name: Combinatorial Eluder Dimension / Projected Distinguishing Range
details: The candidate universal inequality $\mathrm{Edim}\ge\mathrm R^p$ is false. More strongly, no absolute constants C,D give $\mathrm R^p\le C\mathrm{Edim}+D$ on all finite binary classes. The paired-code family has $\mathrm R^p=2^n$ and $\mathrm{Edim}\le8n+3$. The old eight-concept class with values four and five remains a valid strict finite witness. The opposite affine direction is separately refuted by the triangular-code family; the combined affine-incomparability statement is relationship 522. Nonlinear bounds are not excluded.
proof_source: Survey cor:paired-code-range-separation, using prop:paired-code-eluder and the database-owned paired-code values.
witness_verification: The database-owned values give Rp/Edim >= 2^n/(8n+3), which tends to infinity. This is an unbounded ratio of finite values, not a nonexistence convention or merely a growing additive difference. The finite paired-word identities and probabilistic exponent are replayed by sync/verify_paired_code_separation.py.
